title: Google Analytics vs Umami
description: Google Analytics 4 vs Umami — compare free Google analytics vs open-source self-hostable privacy-friendly web analytics.
verdict: Choose Umami when you want open-source, self-hostable (or Umami Cloud) web analytics with a simple dashboard and cookieless options. Choose GA4 when you need free Google ecosystem depth — Ads, Search Console, BigQuery — and can accept cookie/consent complexity.
quickAnswer: **Umami** is the better fit if you want **MIT-licensed, self-hostable analytics** with essential metrics and low ops cost for developers. **Google Analytics 4** is the better fit if you need **free, deep marketing analytics** integrated with Google Ads and warehouses.
bottomLine: Umami wins for technical teams escaping GA4 complexity and ownership concerns. GA4 wins for marketers living in Google’s stack. Non-technical teams who want managed privacy analytics without Docker should prefer Plausible Cloud or Fathom over self-hosted Umami.

faq.question: Is Umami a full GA4 replacement?
faq.answer: For basic traffic reporting, often yes. It does not replace Google Ads linking, BigQuery export, app+web properties, or GA4’s exploratory analysis tools.

faq.question: Is Umami free?
faq.answer: Self-hosted Umami is free software; you pay for hosting. Umami Cloud is a paid managed option. GA4 standard remains free within Google’s limits.

faq.question: Does Umami need cookies?
faq.answer: Umami supports cookieless tracking configurations. Confirm your setup and legal requirements; self-hosting does not automatically equal compliance.

faq.question: Who should not self-host Umami?
faq.answer: Teams without someone to handle deploys, upgrades, backups, and auth hardening. Use Umami Cloud, Plausible, or Fathom instead.

faq.question: How does performance compare?
faq.answer: GA4’s recorded script is heavy on our fixture (~171 KiB transfer, ~+1.16 s overhead). Umami’s script weight is not yet published on AnalyticsVS — treat Umami performance as pending until we record a fixture.

editorialNotes.title: Open source vs free SaaS
editorialNotes.content: GA4 is free as a Google SaaS with Google’s terms and infrastructure. Umami is free as software you operate (or pay Umami Cloud to operate). The cost shift is from vendor subscription to engineering time — or a smaller managed bill.

editorialNotes.title: Scope
editorialNotes.content: Umami intentionally stays narrow: pageviews, referrers, devices, countries, custom events. If you need heatmaps, flags, or warehouse pipelines, pair or pick another tool.
